say: A project folder is the box that holds your files, notes, and history.
A save point is a snapshot of the files, with your note about what changed.
A side copy lets you try a change without touching the main copy.
A ticket is a written request: a bug, a task, or a question.
A change request asks to bring a side copy into the main copy after someone looks at it.
A check is a person, or a robot, saying what is fine and what is not before the change lands.
An open conversation is for questions and ideas that are not a ticket.
A task board lines up tickets in columns such as to do, doing, and done.
Long notes are extra pages of explanation that live next to the project.
A numbered ship is a marked version people can download.
A public site is a web page built from files in the project.
Robots run checks or other jobs when you save or when you press a button.
A robot recipe is the file that says when a robot runs and what it does.
A saved robot file is something a robot kept, such as a report or a built app.
A shipped library is a packaged copy of code other projects can install.
A cloud work room is a computer in the browser with the project already open.
GitHub's helper suggests code inside GitHub. Buddy is not that product.
GitHub lets you try some models next to a project. That does not give you their weights.
A small snippet is one or a few files shared without a full project.
A ping is a message GitHub sends to your address when something happens, such as a new ticket.
Asking with a link means a program can read or change GitHub by calling a web address.
Asking for exact fields lets a program request only the pieces it needs.
The terminal app is the gh command. It talks to GitHub from a keyboard.
The desktop app is GitHub as a program on your computer, without the terminal.
The phone app lets you read tickets and changes on a phone.
A team home holds many projects and the people who work on them.
A group is a named set of people inside the team home.
Who is allowed says who can read, write, or manage a project.
Landing rules can require a check or a review before a change becomes the main copy.
A hidden password is a value robots can use. It should not be written in the project files.
A ship place is a named target, such as a test site or a live site, with its own rules.
The library updater opens change requests when a library you use has a newer version.
The leaked-password finder looks for keys that were saved in the project by mistake.
The risk finder looks through code for known kinds of mistakes.
A public warning tells users about a security hole and the fix.
Charts show activity such as saves and visitors. They are not a grade.
Alerts tell you when someone mentions you or a ticket changes.
Find looks across code, tickets, and change requests.
Pay a maintainer is GitHub's way to fund someone whose project you use.
The app shop lists tools you can add to a project. Read what each one is allowed to do.
House rules say how people should treat each other on the project.
A landing line waits until checks pass, then brings changes in one at a time.
A limited key lets a program act as you, only for the jobs you ticked. Do not paste it in public files.
Who did what is a record of important actions in a team home.
Class assignments hand each student a copy of a starter project.
GitHub's lessons are short courses GitHub hosts. They are not Buddy's boot camp.
A ticket form asks set questions so a new ticket is easier to read.
A deadline bucket groups tickets you want finished together.
A tag is a colored word on a ticket, such as bug or help wanted.
Big files stores large binaries beside the project instead of inside every save.
Company GitHub is the paid plan for a whole company, with extra admin controls.
Robot machines are the computers that run the recipes. GitHub hosts some. You can host your own.
Build proof records how a file was produced so others can check it.
